geos.label: South Bay
geos.blurb: San Jose, Saratoga, Sunnyvale, Mountain View

events.title: San Jose Sharks vs Minnesota Wild
events.note: The first of two home games this week. Downtown San Jose on a Monday, which makes parking easy for once.

events.title: The Rock Orchestra By Candlelight
events.venue: San Jose Center for the Performing Arts
events.note: Rock songs arranged for strings and played by candlelight - a format that has become its own touring industry. No time published.

events.title: Holidays at Filoli: Holiday Daytime
events.note: The house and gardens dressed for the season, daily 10 to 3.30 through 10 January. The glasshouse and the walled garden are the reason to come in daylight rather than for the lights.

events.title: Taste of Filoli Tour
events.note: A guided hour and a half on the estate's kitchens and gardens, with tastings. Also Wednesday at 1.

events.title: Flora Party: Thanksgiving Centerpieces
events.note: Build an arrangement from the cutting garden and take it to dinner. Also twice on Tuesday.

events.title: Holiday Lights at Filoli
events.note: The illuminated garden walk, 4 to 10 nightly through 11 December. Timed entry, and it is cold on that hillside - layers.

events.title: Japanese Tea Garden Free Admission Hour
events.venue: Japanese Tea Garden, Golden Gate Park
events.note: The hour before the gates start charging, and the only hour the garden is quiet. SF residents are free any time with ID.

events.title: Beaver Bauer: From Street to Stage
events.note: Fifty years of costume design, most of it for the Pickle Family Circus and A.C.T. Free, in the Main Library's gallery.

events.title: Nostalgia
events.note: Group show at Mirus, which reliably books the figurative end of the street-adjacent painting world.

events.title: Fernando Carnauba and Albert Dicruttalo: Momentum
events.note: Two sculptors on weight and balance; the Schwartz is one of the few SoMa galleries still keeping full weekday hours.

events.title: Graciela Iturbide: Between Two Worlds
events.note: The biggest Iturbide retrospective yet staged in the US - six decades of Mexican photography that refuses the picturesque. Showing alongside Sarah Sze, Raven Chacon's New Work, Ways of Seeing and the RM x SFMOMA collaboration. Closed Wednesday, open till 8 on Thanksgiving.

events.title: Vishnu's Cosmic Ocean
events.note: Hindu cosmology through sculpture and painting, paired this month with the Ha Chong-Hyun retrospective - the Korean dansaekhwa painter who pushed pigment through the back of the canvas. Open till 8 on Thursday.

events.title: Siddharth Parasnis: Conversation in Color
events.note: Bay Area painter whose blocky architectural canvases sit somewhere between Diebenkorn and a Mumbai street.

events.title: Ray Kleinlein: Recent Paintings
events.note: Still lifes of studio detritus, shown with Andrea Way's Rhapsodies in Blue. Closed Monday and across the Thanksgiving weekend - Tuesday and Wednesday are your window.

events.title: Glow: Play in the Light
events.note: The Exploratorium's light-and-perception hall, which is the part of the building adults linger in longest.

events.title: Awaking Beauty: The Art of Eyvind Earle
events.note: The designer who gave Sleeping Beauty its flat, tapestry-like world against the studio's house style, and won.

events.title: No Punk. No Future.
events.note: West German punk as documentary record - flyers, fanzines, Super 8. Weekdays only.

events.title: Holiday Ice Rink in Union Square
events.note: Open daily to 11pm. Free on Thanksgiving Day itself, and there is a free learn-to-skate session at 8am on weekend mornings.

events.title: Nintendo San Francisco Holiday Decor
events.note: Free holiday build-out at the Powell Street store. Listed because it is free and the children will not care that it is also a shop.

events.title: Robert Adams: Contact
events.note: The photographer who made the American West look exactly as developed as it is. Contact prints, small and unsparing.

events.title: Deborah Butterfield: New Work
events.note: Horses built from found wood and cast in bronze so the wood survives. At Haines' Fort Mason space.

events.title: Forecast 2026
events.note: Camerawork's annual survey of what Bay Area photographers are actually making, which is usually the least settled show in the city.

events.title: Chuck Sperry: Archetypes
events.note: The poster artist's hand-pulled goddesses, at gallery scale rather than gig-flyer scale.

events.title: Sideways Glance
events.note: Slash Art's group show; the gallery runs on artist residencies, so the work tends to be newer than the market.

events.title: Invaders: Vallejo, Food and the Making of California
events.note: The di Rosa collection's new city outpost, on Mariano Vallejo and how California's food system was built on the land he lost.

events.title: Syd Mead: Future Pastime
events.note: The concept artist who drew Blade Runner's Los Angeles and Tron's grid. Ground-floor gallery, through 17 December.

events.title: FOR-SITE: Attentive Earth
events.note: Muzae Sesay and Alexcia Sundra in the Guardhouse, with Leah Rosenberg's The Sea Is But Another Sky and the American Indian Cultural District's We Are The Land across the campus. All free.

events.title: Karla Knight: Fine Tuner
events.note: Invented alphabets and spacecraft diagrams painted with the patience of a medieval scribe.

events.title: Max Jansons: Project Room
events.note: Shown with Simon Evans and Sarah Lannan's Never Better Than Later. Both through 19 December.

events.title: Dorian Reid: Calling All Cats!
events.note: MoAD's current solo: Reid's cats are a device for talking about Black domestic interiors.

events.title: Chris Natrop
events.note: Cut-paper installations that read as light rather than object. Minnesota Street Project.

events.title: Protobyte Phylogeny
events.note: Ira Greenberg's generative-form installation, running to January. Gray Area has no performance this week, which is unusual for it.

events.title: OBJECTS: USA
events.note: The long-running survey of American studio craft, which is where the line between furniture and sculpture gets argued.

events.title: Land / Water / Meat / Noise
events.note: Southern Exposure's group show on extraction and the sounds it makes. Free, Mission Street.

events.title: Leila Weefur: The Chapel of Becoming
events.note: Video and sound installation at The Lab, whose Redstone Building room is itself worth the trip. Free.

events.title: SF SPCA Holiday Windows
events.note: Adoptable puppies and kittens in the Union Square windows, daily through the holidays. A civic institution, free, and the queue moves.

events.title: Larisa Brechun: Somnia
events.note: Dream-logic figuration in a small Sutter Street room. Open afternoons only.

events.title: Lightscape at the Botanical Garden
events.note: The illuminated trail through Golden Gate Park's garden, nightly 5 to 8.15. Timed entry; it sells out at weekends and the fog improves it.

events.title: Ode to Joy: European CineFest
events.note: Two free screenings - Dolph: Unbreakable at 5.30 and A Memoria do Cheiro das Coisas at 7.30 - in the EU consulates' annual festival. RSVP required.

events.title: Dark Habits
events.note: Almodovar's convent comedy, in the Roxie's In the Mood for Almodovar series.

events.title: SalsaCrazy Mondays
events.note: Classes from 6.30, then salsa and bachata social until close. Beginners are the point rather than tolerated.

events.title: Who Killed Alex Odeh?
events.note: Documentary on the 1985 killing of the Arab-American Anti-Discrimination Committee organiser, still unsolved.

events.title: Motown on Mondays
events.note: Soul 45s on a Monday, and the reason the Madrone has a dance floor at all. Free if you get there before eight.

events.title: Sound Baths at Grace Cathedral
events.note: Gongs and singing bowls under the nave's stone, which does most of the work. Ninety minutes flat on your back.

events.title: An Evening in Conversation with Dusty Baker
events.note: The Giants' former manager on a long playing and managing career. Steep for a talk, but the ticket carries a signed book and a bottle.

events.title: Hayes Valley Comedy Night
events.note: The Function's nightly free showcase. Two-drink minimum, which is how it stays free.

events.title: La Bola Negra
events.note: Spanish-language feature in the Castro's new programming run; doors 6.30. Sold out here, and playing the Roxie all week if you miss it.

events.title: CocoRosie
events.note: The Casady sisters' freak-folk: toy pianos and opera training rubbing against nursery-rhyme menace. Twenty years on it still sounds like nothing else. The Fillmore publishes no door time.

events.title: Gary Numan
events.note: The man who put the synthesiser at the front of a pop record in 1979 and has spent the last decade making industrial albums rather than nostalgia sets. Expect the new material alongside the two songs everyone came for.

events.title: Mirthquake: Monday Live Comedy in the Richmond
events.note: Neighbourhood stand-up in a Clement Street pub, $5 drinks, no pretension.

events.title: Pedro the Lion
events.note: Slowcore built on David Bazan's flat, unhurried delivery and a Christianity he spent two decades arguing with rather than leaving. Karli Fairbanks opens. Sold out, and one of the last Mondays for a room that closes at the end of 2026.

events.title: The Host (4K Restoration)
events.note: Bong Joon-ho restored - the one where the Han River creature is the least frightening thing on screen.

events.title: On the Road (En el Camino)
events.note: Mexican road feature, playing all week at the Roxie.

events.title: Krazy For Karaoke
events.note: The Knockout's standing Monday: karaoke with a bar's worth of regulars who treat it as a performance slot rather than a lark.

events.title: Monday Night Hubba
events.note: Hubba Hubba Revue's weekly burlesque and variety hour, before Death Guild takes the floor.

events.title: Death Guild
events.note: The longest-running goth-industrial night in the country, Mondays since 1993. Read off SF Station - DNA's own calendar refuses this run by name.

events.title: Song Dongye
events.note: Chinese singer-songwriter whose plain-spoken Beijing folk made him a generational voice at home; a rare US date. On the Songkick sweep only - the Warfield's own calendar shows nothing before 4 December, so treat the date as unconfirmed.

events.title: Town Biz Comedy Night
events.note: HellaFunny's free Monday and Tuesday showcase in Temescal. Food and drink for sale, comedy free.

events.title: Back to the Future Thanksgiving Celebration
events.note: Memphis singer Lawrence Matthews with Derrick Hall & Company - a soul revue rather than a tribute set. Yoshi's is a listening room, so the band will be audible.

events.title: Rishab Rikhiram Sharma: Sitar For Mental Health
events.note: Ravi Shankar's last student playing sitar in the Paramount's art-deco hall, with mental health as the evening's stated subject. The building alone justifies the ticket. No time published.

events.title: Pher the Legend
events.note: With Wake Naked and DJs Mellow Brown and Ramilio, in a 150-capacity Albany room.

events.title: Garden of d'Lights
events.note: The dry garden lit up after dark, which does strange and good things to a succulent collection. BART plus a short ride gets you there.

events.title: Crossroads Showcase
events.note: A young-bands showcase, doors 5. Recorded rather than recommended.

events.title: Pearl Charles
events.note: Cosmic country in a Santa Cruz creperie. From the Songkick sweep.

events.title: Cityline Holiday Ice Skating Under the Redwoods
events.note: An outdoor rink under the redwoods in downtown Sunnyvale, walkable from Caltrain.

events.title: Psycroptic
events.note: Tasmanian technical death metal with Inferi, Cognitive and Summoning The Lich. Four bands, doors 6.30.

events.title: MLS Cup First Round: San Jose Earthquakes vs Houston Dynamo
events.venue: Habbas Law Epicenter at PayPal Park
events.note: A home playoff game for the Earthquakes, which has not been a sentence anyone could write for some years. VTA Fruitdale and a fifteen-minute walk, $25 to park.

events.title: IlluminOdyssey 10
events.note: A glowing walk-through science installation at the Coyote Point museum, through 24 January. Members free, and the animal exhibits are included.

events.title: Filoli Unwrapped
events.note: An hour on how the holiday installation is actually built, which is the most interesting tour the estate runs. Daily at 11 from Friday.

events.title: Fall Holiday Farmers Market
events.note: The Tuesday Ferry Plaza market, extended for the Thanksgiving run. Get there before noon if you want the brussels sprouts.

events.title: Build with LEGO Master Tim Hutchins
events.note: A certified LEGO professional building in public at the Brick Exhibition. For children, and for the kind of adult who will not admit it.

events.title: Full Moon Community Art and Wellness Fest
events.note: Free all-ages gathering in the newly rebuilt Bayview park - art tables, bodywork, music till dark. The park itself is the draw.

events.title: Noe Valley Night Market
events.note: Makers and food stalls on the square, 5 to 8. Posted one date at a time, so do not assume it recurs.

events.title: After-Hours Yoga in the Conservatory
events.note: Yoga under glass after the garden closes, on the same nights as Lightscape - the two do not conflict.

events.title: Yoga on the Labyrinth
events.note: Tuesday-evening practice on the cathedral labyrinth, with the organ. Also Saturday at 9am.

events.title: John Proctor Is the Villain
events.note: Kimberly Belflower's Georgia high-school Crucible, the most talked-about new American play of the season. A post-show conversation follows tonight.

events.title: The Amity Affliction
events.note: Australian metalcore with blessthefall, Orthodox and Buried In Spring under them - a four-band bill that will run long. Orthodox is the set worth arriving for.

events.title: Sylvia Black
events.note: Los Angeles goth exotica - torch singing over drum machines - with The Poor Luckies and XOX. DICE lists the night twice under two ticket links; it is one show.

events.title: Peter Pan Goes Wrong
events.note: Mischief Theatre's pantomime catastrophe, in its final week after a two-month run. Funcheap carries a $5-off code.

events.title: Texas Tuesdays: Line Dancing with Cassaundra
events.note: Lessons then open floor in the Cigar Bar's courtyard, which is heated and covered.

events.title: SF History Night: Pacific Heights
events.note: The Historical Society's neighbourhood series, on the hill the 1906 fire stopped at. Ten dollars.

events.title: Tim Burton's The Nightmare Before Christmas in Concert
events.note: The film with Danny Elfman's score played live by the San Francisco Symphony. Sold out, and the first of three film-with-orchestra nights at Davies this week.

events.title: Punch Line Secret Guest List: Joe Klocek and Friends
events.note: The Punch Line's midweek industry showcase. Free if you RSVP and arrive half an hour early; 18+, two-drink minimum.

events.title: Hayes Valley Comedy Night
events.note: The Tuesday edition of the Function's free nightly showcase.

events.title: The Music of Hey Arnold! Live
events.note: Jim Lang and the PS 118 AllStars playing the cartoon's jazz cues, with creator Craig Bartlett in the room. Night one is sold out; Wednesday still has tickets.

events.title: Kilowatt Karaoke
events.note: The Mission bar's Tuesday karaoke, now ticketed through DICE, which tells you how full it gets.

events.title: Steve Lacy
events.note: First of two nights. The Internet's guitarist turned solo act, still writing bedroom-recorded funk and then playing it to 7,000 people. No door time published.

events.title: Karaoke at the Madrone
events.note: Tuesday karaoke, running alongside the live-model sketch session in the front room.

events.title: Live Model Tuesday Sketch
events.note: Bring a pad; a model holds poses while the bar carries on around you. The most Divisadero thing in the listing.

events.title: Maren Hassinger: Living Moving Growing
events.note: Five decades of sculpture made from wire rope, branches and plastic bags, shown with Some Particular Heaven from the BAMPFA collection. Free docent tours Wednesday at 12.15 and Sunday at 2. Galleries close at 5 this week and the museum is shut on Thanksgiving.

events.title: Liberation (matinee)
events.note: Bess Wohl's play about a 1970s consciousness-raising group, told by a daughter trying to reconstruct it. West Coast premiere, closing Sunday.

events.title: Mezcal and Mole Comedy Night
events.note: Tuesday edition.

events.title: Liberation
events.note: Tuesday evening.

events.title: Last Tuesdays Comedy
events.note: Monthly stand-up in a downtown Oakland bar. Transit is the sensible way in - most downtown garages shut their gates at seven.

events.title: $6 Drive-In Movie Night
events.note: The standing Tuesday six-dollar night at one of the last drive-ins in the region.

events.title: Tito Puente Jr.
events.note: The son carrying the father's band book, with flautist Nestor Torres. A seated listening room is an odd home for mambo and it works better than it should.

events.title: Open Mic Night with Caroline DeLone
events.note: Free, all comers.

events.title: Phil Johnson
events.note: Comedy in Mill Valley; from the Songkick sweep.

events.title: Give Thanks Festival
events.note: A four-day indoor EDM festival over the holiday weekend, with Seven Lions, SLANDER, Said the Sky and TYNAN across the bill. 18+. The ticketing splits it into a Wednesday night and a Friday-Saturday main event, and no source publishes the day-by-day lineup cleanly.

events.title: San Jose Barracuda vs Coachella Valley Firebirds
events.note: AHL hockey next door to the SAP Center, which is the cheap and much more watchable version of Monday night.

events.title: Clue: Live On Stage
events.note: The board game as a farce, staged by Kenneth Kelleher for the holidays. The company publishes no per-date times; this Wednesday show is confirmed by the Hammer Theatre's listing feed.

events.title: Los Gemelos de Sinaloa
events.note: Sierreno duo in a 3,000-seat hall on Thanksgiving eve - the regional-Mexican circuit treats this week as a peak, and the Civic has two of its bills.

events.title: Jeff Dean
events.note: One show on Thanksgiving eve.

events.title: Roosters Comedy Showcase
events.note: The Sunnyvale club's midweek showcase; the Songkick sweep names Greg Capra on the bill, the club's own page names nobody.

events.title: Roberto Tapia
events.note: Banda and norteno on a four-act Thanksgiving-eve bill with Grupo H-100, Conjunto Ave Nortena and Banda Exclusiva.

events.title: Banda Tierra Menguarense and Graciela Beltran
events.note: From the Songkick sweep; the venue publishes nothing a fetch can read.

events.title: Incredible Sugar Castle
events.note: The hotel pastry team's annual sugar architecture in the lobby. Free, absurd, and up through the holidays.

events.title: Japanese Tea Garden Free Admission Hour
events.venue: Japanese Tea Garden, Golden Gate Park
events.note: The Wednesday free hour.

events.title: YBCA Free Admission Day
events.venue: Yerba Buena Center for the Arts
events.note: Every Wednesday the galleries are free: GaHee Park's Behind the Curtain, Rael San Fratello's Prototypes and Provocations, and Dread Scott's The Body Politic. Scott is the one to see.

events.title: Peter Pan Goes Wrong (matinee)
events.note: Wednesday matinee in the closing week.

events.title: John Proctor Is the Villain (matinee)
events.note: Matinee with a post-show conversation at 2.

events.title: Dear San Francisco (matinee)
events.note: The 7 Fingers' acrobatic love letter to the city, in its holiday run. The North Beach room has been doing variety since the Beach Blanket days.

events.title: Untypical Girl Rock n' Roll Happy Hour
events.note: An early record-spinning set before the dance party, run by and for women in the local rock scene.

events.title: On the Road (En el Camino)
events.note: Continuing at the Roxie.

events.title: Fatherland
events.note: Documentary on an inheritance of political violence.

events.title: The Wrecks
events.note: Los Angeles rock band on the Finally OUTSIDE tour, with Worry Club and Kid Sistr. A young room.

events.title: Plaster, Lil Dude & The Dorks and HeyKujo & The Homies
events.note: Three local bands in a 150-capacity bar on the night nobody works the next morning. The bill is scrappier than the room.

events.title: Peter Pan Goes Wrong
events.note: Evening performance, closing week.

events.title: Aura at Grace Cathedral
events.note: Light-and-sound installation filling the nave, two sittings a night. The building does half the work and the projection the rest.

events.title: The Super Shangri-La Show
events.note: The Balboa's long-running variety-and-film night in the Richmond - a neighbourhood cinema programming like a club.

events.title: Golden State Warriors vs Sacramento Kings
events.note: The only Warriors home game before the weekend. Arena basketball, listed for completeness.

events.title: Cobb's Secret Guest List
events.note: North Beach's big comedy room, free on the guest list. 18+, two-drink minimum.

events.title: Thanksgiving Eve Queer Comedy and Friendsgiving
events.note: Comedy and a potluck in the Eagle's yard. Listed free with a suggested donation, which is how the Eagle does everything.

events.title: John Proctor Is the Villain
events.note: Evening performance.

events.title: Dear San Francisco
events.note: Evening performance.

events.title: FREE Comedy Night at The Function
events.note: Wednesday edition.

events.title: Cheaper Than Therapy
events.note: The city's most reliable stand-up night, in a 90-seat Sutter Street theatre. Runs Wednesday through Sunday.

events.title: Andre Nickatina
events.note: Thirty years of Fillmore-district rap delivered in that clipped, unhurried cadence nobody has successfully copied. A hometown Thanksgiving-eve ritual; doors 7.

events.title: Moonalice
events.note: Bay Area jam-rock with the Mad Alchemy Liquid Light Show doing the oil-projector work behind them. All ages, doors 7 - and the band plays Felton on Friday and Mill Valley on Sunday, so there is no need to drive.

events.title: ovrkast.
events.note: Oakland producer-rapper whose beats sit under the vocal rather than behind it - the Still Striking tour. All ages, doors 7.

events.title: 1 Umbrella
events.note: The DHS Tour. No support listed, which at the Independent usually means a long single set.

events.title: The Music of Hey Arnold! Live
events.note: Second night, and the one still on sale. Doors 7.

events.title: SpudsGiving 2
events.price: no cover, pay what you want
events.note: A free baked-potato bar and vinyl DJs in a Bernal dive on the night before Thanksgiving. Exactly as good as it sounds. 21+.

events.title: Raise the Red Lantern (4K Restoration)
events.note: Zhang Yimou's 1991 picture of a concubine household, restored. The most beautiful thing on a Bay Area screen this week.

events.title: La Bola Negra
events.note: Also at the Castro on Monday, and sold out there.

events.title: Friendsgiving Ice Skating Night
events.note: A late session with the rink mostly to yourselves.

events.title: Cumbia and Oldies Dance Party
events.note: The Knockout's best-attended standing night: cumbia rebajada into lowrider oldies, and the floor fills by eleven.

events.title: SF Goth Holiday Ball
events.note: The city's goth scene's annual dress-up, found on SF Station because DNA's own calendar will not answer this run.

events.title: Andy C
events.note: Thirty years of drum and bass from the man who turned the double-drop into a signature. 1015's Thanksgiving-eve booking, and the biggest club night of the week.

events.title: Steve Lacy
events.note: Second of two nights at the Civic.

events.title: Nino Msk
events.note: From the Songkick sweep; the Make-Out Room publishes no times in advance.

events.title: Joshua Iz, 3kelves and Huffy
events.note: Deep house downstairs at Monarch, which is the most consistently well-booked small basement in SoMa.

events.title: Shake & Pop
events.note: Thanksgiving-eve DJ night at the Madrone.

events.title: Macy Blackman
events.note: New Orleans piano and jump blues. The calendar places this on the 25th but its own link is dated the 19th - worth a call before you go.

events.title: Covenant
events.note: York Walker's West Coast premiere - a Georgia town, a bluesman back from nowhere, and a rumour about what he traded. Berkeley Rep's own site would not load for this run, so the date comes from resale listings; confirm with the box office.

events.title: Free Oakland Thanksgiving Eve Comedy Night
events.note: Temescal's Thanksgiving-eve showcase, free in.

events.title: Liberation
events.note: Wednesday evening.

events.title: Irish Christmas in America
events.note: A touring trad show built around the Irish midwinter rather than the American one - pipes, fiddle, step dance, and no sleigh bells.

events.title: Gretchen Menn
events.note: Instrumental guitar composition rather than shredding, with Daniele Gottardo, Michael Manring on bass and Scott Amendola on drums. On paper the most technically serious band in a small room this week.

events.title: The Egg
events.note: From the Songkick sweep; Thee Stork Club's own calendar read empty this run.

events.title: Los Caimanes De Sinaloa, Banda La Fantastica and Banda la Lujosa
events.note: Three bandas on a Thanksgiving-eve bill in Concord. These rooms rarely reach an aggregator, and this one only did through Songkick.

events.title: Blackout Wednesday with DJ Sardine
events.note: In the Catalyst Atrium, 18+.

events.title: Vinyl's Annual Black Wednesday Bash
events.note: Marin's Thanksgiving-eve tradition. Sold out, doors 7.

events.title: Country For A Cause
events.note: The Henry Warde Band benefiting the Second Harvest Food Bank.

events.title: Open Mic Night
events.note: Free; from the Songkick sweep.

events.title: Indigenous Peoples' Sunrise Ceremony
events.note: The annual gathering on Alcatraz at dawn on Thanksgiving morning, marking the 1969-71 occupation. Boats leave Pier 33 from about 4.15am and it is over by eight. Cold, crowded, and the single most significant thing happening in the Bay Area this week.

events.title: SF's Free-ish Turkey Trot
events.price: free with a donation of new socks
events.note: A run through the park whose entry fee is a pair of new socks for a shelter. No timing chip, no expo.

events.title: Thanksgiving Day Ice Skating
events.note: The rink is free all Thanksgiving Day. The best free thing in the city on a day when very little is open.

events.title: Walking Tour: Welcome to San Francisco
events.note: Downtown SF's guided introduction, running on the holiday.

events.title: Community Thanksgiving Potluck
events.note: Open table in the Castro, noon to three, bring a dish if you can. RSVP so they can count plates.

events.title: After Dark at the Exploratorium
events.note: The 18-and-over evening at the Exploratorium, running on Thanksgiving itself. The Glow hall after a large meal is the right order of operations.

events.title: Peter Pan Goes Wrong
events.note: Thanksgiving-night performance taken from the standing weekly schedule; the Playhouse warns that showtimes vary and no aggregator confirms this one. Ring the box office first.

events.title: Flight Club at House of Air
events.note: Adults-only trampoline hour in the Presidio hangar, 18+. Grip socks required.

events.title: Black Ass Weekend 2026
events.note: Three days of Black queer burlesque and drag at Oasis, opening Thanksgiving night. 21+, two-drink minimum.

events.title: Thanksgiving Night 'Turkey'oke
events.note: The Knockout's annual Thanksgiving karaoke sing-fest, which has the quality of a family gathering you chose.

events.title: A Rashomon
events.note: New work at the Magic, which stages on Thanksgiving night when almost nobody else does. The Fort Mason company's remit is premieres only.

events.title: Jack Kays and His Band
events.note: The only real Thanksgiving-night rock show in the city. Found on SF Station - the Independent's own calendar does not list it.

events.title: 16th & Mission Open Mic
events.note: The plaza open mic that has run without a microphone for years. Free, late, and entirely itself.

events.title: Inner Circle Dance Party
events.note: Thursday standing night, free on the list.

events.title: Indigenous Freedom Quiz Contest
events.price: free, donations to the Mohawk Freedom School
events.note: A free quiz with hundred-dollar cash prizes on Thanksgiving afternoon, the proceeds going to a Mohawk-language school. The counter-programming of the week.

events.title: SJ Made Holiday Craft Fair
events.note: Three hundred and fifty makers over two days, free to get in and free to park, with a tote for the first thousand through the door each day. The best free thing in the South Bay this week.

events.title: San Jose State Spartans Football
events.note: A midday Black Friday kickoff on campus.

events.title: San Jose Sharks vs Vegas Golden Knights
events.note: A one-o'clock Black Friday start, billed as Youth Hockey Appreciation. Early enough to be a family afternoon.

events.title: Clue: Live On Stage
events.note: Date from an aggregator; the company publishes no schedule a fetch can read.

events.title: Chris Porter
events.note: Two shows, 7.30 and 9.45; four across the weekend.

events.title: Merry-Achi Christmas
events.note: Mariachi Sol de Mexico's Christmas show, three performances over the weekend. The Hammer's own calendar is drawn by a widget a fetch cannot read; this comes from sanjose.events.

events.title: The 1940s Radio Hour
events.note: A wartime radio broadcast staged live, which is a sturdier device than it sounds and lets a small company use a big band.

events.title: Arabic Thanksgiving
events.note: Arabic pop and dabke, 21+.

events.title: Mariachi Nuevo Tecalitlán
events.note: Billed with Mariachi Vargas de Tecalitlan, the oldest continuously performing mariachi in the world and the ensemble every other one is measured against. If that billing holds it is the most significant concert in the South Bay this week.

events.title: The Carpenters Songbook: At Christmas
events.venue: San Jose Center for the Performing Arts
events.note: A one-night add-on to the Broadway San Jose season.

events.title: Satori
events.note: Organic house. From the Songkick sweep; the Ritz's Live Nation page does not list it.

events.title: Mr V
events.note: New York house veteran in a small San Jose bar.

events.title: Give Thanks Festival
